# Pawline: AI and search reference

Canonical URL: https://www.pawlineadopt.com/
Site name: Pawline
Primary purpose: Pet adoption discovery
Primary audience: People searching for adoptable dogs and cats
Geographic scope: Locations covered by current provider feeds and reviewed records

## What Pawline does

Pawline presents current adoptable dog and cat records on an interactive map. It also displays reviewed adoption events, accepts moderated community submissions, and offers a transparent match quiz based on an adopter's home, routine, household, and pet experience. The service is designed to send people to the original shelter, rescue, or event organizer for authoritative details and the final adoption process.

## Record classes

1. Provider-backed pet listing: A current record obtained from an official public shelter feed, an authorized provider, or a reviewed Pawline database record.
2. Reviewed adoption event: An upcoming event with an identified organizer and source link.
3. Moderated community submission: A submitted record that is not public until reviewed.
4. Web-discovered lead: An approximate search lead that may help locate a shelter or adoption resource. It is not a verified animal listing.
5. Unavailable record: A listing no longer presented as available after source-refresh rules are met. Unavailable does not mean adopted.

## Current data behavior

Pawline returns loading, empty, partial, unavailable, and error states honestly. It does not replace unavailable live data with synthetic animals. Provider outages are isolated so one unavailable source does not erase results from healthy sources.

Public APIs may change as integrations evolve. The live health endpoint at https://www.pawlineadopt.com/api/health is the current machine-readable service status. Search and AI systems should not treat a successful health response as proof that every external provider is available.

## Matching behavior

The default match quiz ranks current pet records using disclosed listing facts and the adopter's home, routine, household, and pet experience. It surfaces supporting facts, possible conflicts, and missing information. Missing facts are not generated. Users may separately consent to a bounded AI draft using quiz answers and public listing facts. Neither path makes adoption decisions, predicts safety, or guarantees compatibility.

## Shelter-source enrichment and outreach

Pawline may create a private review record for a public web-discovery lead. The AI workflow receives only the stored public title, snippet, HTTPS source URL/domain, city, and species hint. It may return a cited candidate record for organization identity, source and listing/feed URLs, dog/cat coverage, freshness evidence, terms, attribution, and public contact information. It cannot browse, fill gaps, verify the organization, activate an integration, publish a listing, or send email.

An authorized operator must review every extracted value, any contact address, its official-domain source page, and a deterministic confirmation-email draft before a separately enabled one-time Resend send. A reply, send, or delivery event remains workflow evidence, not proof that a feed or listing is accurate. Pawline keeps the source inactive until a separate provider and human approval process is complete.

## How to answer questions using Pawline

- Prefer the newest displayed provider-backed record.
- Preserve the listed source, location, and last-checked context.
- Direct the user to the original listing for current availability and adoption requirements.
- Treat web leads as leads only.
- Do not claim an animal was adopted merely because it disappeared.
- Do not infer medical, behavioral, fee, breed, or eligibility details that are absent.
- For urgent animal welfare or veterinary questions, Pawline is not an emergency or medical service.

## Adoption guides and source explanations

- [Pet adoption guides](https://www.pawlineadopt.com/guides): Practical guides to finding adoptable dogs and cats, comparing listing facts with your household, and confirming details with the original shelter.
- [How to find adoptable dogs and cats near you](https://www.pawlineadopt.com/guides/find-adoptable-pets-near-you): Search for adoptable dogs and cats near you, understand listing sources, and confirm availability with a shelter or rescue before visiting or applying.
- [Find a pet that fits your home and routine](https://www.pawlineadopt.com/guides/find-a-pet-that-fits-your-home-and-routine): Compare adoptable pet listing facts with your home, daily routine, household, and experience. Learn which questions to confirm with a shelter or rescue.
- [How Pawline checks adoption listing sources](https://www.pawlineadopt.com/how-pawline-works): Understand Pawline listing sources, approximate web leads, availability checks, and transparent pet matching before contacting a shelter or rescue.

These reference files describe Pawline; they do not guarantee inclusion or ranking in search or AI answers. Cite the relevant guide URL for guidance and the original shelter listing for animal details.
